issue.title: Enhancement: [test_auto_techsupport] test_max_limit testcase fix on container unexpected dump size

failure.body:
### Description of the enhancement

show_techsupport/test_auto_techsupport.py on  test_max_limit
TestAutoTechSupport test_max_limit AssertionError with
Expected file: ...tar.gz not found in available files list

adding auto-tech since option from 2 days ago(default) to 1hr

**Is it platform specific**
generic

**Importance or Severity**
Critical

**info**
the reason is that below is the testcase flow:
Test logic is as follows:

Set core/techsupport max limit to 0
Create 4 core/techsupport dummy files(each file 5%) which will use 20% of space in test folder
Trigger techsupport and check that dummy files + new created core/techsupport files available
Set core/techsupport max limit to 14
Trigger techsupport and check that 2 oldest dummy files removed, all other + new created core/techsupport
from 20% to 14%, it means the testcase expected to remove original 2 files at least.
however, except for 4 x5% dumpfiles, testcase also triggers 2 coredumps from random containers which can not expect these new core dump size always below than 5%.
this is the reason DUT removes all 3 or 4 files (3 or 4 *5%) to keep below than 14%.

resolution.title: [test_auto_techsupport] Fix test_max_limit flakiness with dynamic cleanup validation
resolution.description:
### Description of PR

Summary:
Fixes #21059
Fixes aristanetworks/sonic-qual.msft#1239

`test_max_limit` hardcodes that exactly 2 dummy files will be deleted after triggering cleanup at a 14% storage limit. This assumption breaks when the generated techsupport files are
larger than ~503 MiB, causing 3+ deletions instead of 2 and failing the test.

Root cause: on devices rebooted within the last hour by a prior test (e.g. `sflow/testRebootSflowEnable`), the `--since 1h` window (added by #21823) still captures all intensive
post-boot activity, producing large techsupport files. The `--since 1h` fix alone is not sufficient for this scenario.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] Testbed and Framework(new/improvement)
- [ ] New Test case
    - [ ] Skipped for non-supported platforms
- [x] Test case improvement

### Back port request
- [ ] 202205
- [ ] 202305
- [ ] 202311
- [ ] 202405
- [x] 202411
- [x] 202505
- [x] 202511

### Approach
#### What is the motivation for this PR?
The test fails intermittently when a prior test (e.g. sflow reboot) runs on the same device as `test_auto_techsupport`. After the reboot, intensive post-boot activity fills the
`--since 1h` window producing large techsupport files, pushing total `/var/dump` usage high enough that the cleanup algorithm deletes 3 dummy files instead of the hardcoded
expectation of 2.

See [#21059](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/issues/21059) for full context.

#### How did you do it?
- Added `get_files_info()` helper to query actual file state (name, size, mtime) after cleanup runs.
- Replaced the hardcoded `dummy_files_list[2:]` / `dummy_files_list[:2]` expectations with dynamic calculation: queries remaining files post-cleanup, finds the oldest surviving dummy
index, and derives expected/not-expected lists from that. The meaningful assertions are fully preserved:
  - Oldest-first deletion order (`not_expected_stub_files`)
  - Total file count (`expected_number_of_additional_files=2`)
  - Folder size within limit (`expected_max_folder_size`)

#### How did you verify/test it?
Verified on dualtor topologies. `test_max_limit[techsupport]` passes with the fix applied.
